bp_systolic.name: Blood pressure (top number)
bp_systolic.why_it_matters: High pressure makes your heart and blood vessels work harder.
bp_systolic.what_to_do_yellow: Rest 5 minutes and measure again. One reading alone is not a reason to worry.
bp_systolic.what_to_do_red: Measure again after 5 minutes of rest. If it is still red, Maia alerts your medical team. If you have chest pain, trouble breathing, weakness or trouble speaking, open the guide now.
bp_systolic.source: S27; S28; S48 (space technique: demo); S61; S62

bp_diastolic.name: Blood pressure (bottom number)
bp_diastolic.why_it_matters: The bottom number shows the pressure while your heart rests between beats.
bp_diastolic.what_to_do_red: Measure again after 5 minutes of rest. If it is still red, Maia alerts your medical team.

heart_rate.name: Resting heart rate
heart_rate.why_it_matters: A higher resting pulse can be a sign of poor sleep, illness or not enough water.
heart_rate.what_to_do_yellow: Rest, drink water and measure again in 5 minutes.
heart_rate.what_to_do_red: If you feel your heart racing, dizzy or faint, stop and open the guide. Maia alerts your medical team.

spo2.name: Oxygen (SpO₂)
spo2.why_it_matters: Shows how much oxygen your blood is carrying.
spo2.what_to_do_yellow: Warm your hand, keep still and measure again in 5 minutes. If you feel short of breath, trust how you feel even if the number looks normal.
spo2.what_to_do_red: Sit up, breathe slowly and open the guide. Maia alerts your medical team.
spo2.source: S32; S48 (oximeter accuracy note); S61; S62

temperature.name: Body temperature
temperature.why_it_matters: A rise can mean infection or heat stress. In space your normal temperature slowly goes up about 1 °C, so Maia compares you with your own normal.
temperature.what_to_do_yellow: Rest, drink water and measure again in 15 minutes.
temperature.what_to_do_red: Stop exercise, cool down, drink water and open the guide. Maia alerts your medical team.

body_mass.name: Body mass
body_mass.why_it_matters: Losing mass can mean you are not eating or drinking enough.
body_mass.what_to_do_yellow: Check what you ate and drank this week.
body_mass.what_to_do_red: Tell your medical team; Maia sends the trend.

sleep.name: Sleep
sleep.why_it_matters: Short sleep lowers attention and mood and makes mistakes more likely.
sleep.what_to_do_yellow: Keep your sleep time free, dim the lights before bed.
sleep.what_to_do_red: If you slept under 6 hours for 2 nights, avoid critical tasks and tell your medical team.

ecg_qtc.name: Heart rhythm (ECG)
ecg_qtc.why_it_matters: Shows if your heartbeat is regular.
ecg_qtc.what_to_do_yellow: Rest and record again. Note any palpitations.
ecg_qtc.what_to_do_red: If your heart feels irregular with dizziness or chest pain, open the guide.

respiratory_rate.name: Breathing rate
respiratory_rate.why_it_matters: Fast breathing can be an early sign of a breathing or heart problem.
respiratory_rate.what_to_do_yellow: Rest and count again in 5 minutes.
respiratory_rate.what_to_do_red: Sit up, check oxygen and open the guide.

glucose.name: Blood sugar (fasting)
glucose.why_it_matters: Long missions may change how your body uses sugar.
glucose.what_to_do_yellow: If it is low (54–69), eat or drink fast sugar and measure again in 15 minutes. If it is high, measure again tomorrow.
glucose.what_to_do_red: If it is under 54, take fast sugar now and tell a crewmate. If it is high, Maia alerts your medical team.

cognition_pvt.name: Attention test (3 min)
cognition_pvt.why_it_matters: Tiredness can slow you down without you noticing.
cognition_pvt.what_to_do_yellow: Rest or sleep before a critical task if you can. Check cabin CO₂.
cognition_pvt.what_to_do_red: Postpone critical tasks if possible and tell your medical team.

radiation_dose.name: Radiation dose
radiation_dose.why_it_matters: Radiation adds up over your career and raises long-term cancer risk.
radiation_dose.what_to_do_yellow: Keep exposure as low as you can: limit time in less shielded areas.
radiation_dose.what_to_do_red: Tell your medical team. Follow shelter instructions during a solar storm.

hydration_urine.name: Hydration (urine colour)
hydration_urine.why_it_matters: Not drinking enough raises the risk of kidney stones and makes you dizzy.
hydration_urine.what_to_do_yellow: Drink a glass of water now and another within the hour.
hydration_urine.what_to_do_red: Drink now, rest, and tell your medical team if you feel dizzy or confused.

bone_density.name: Bone density
bone_density.why_it_matters: Bones lose 1–1.5% of their mineral each month in space.
bone_density.what_to_do_yellow: Keep up resistance exercise, calcium and vitamin D as advised.
bone_density.what_to_do_red: Your medical team will plan your recovery.

vision_acuity.name: Vision check
vision_acuity.why_it_matters: Space can change the shape of the eye (SANS).
vision_acuity.what_to_do_yellow: Measure again in a few days. Note blurred vision or wavy lines.
vision_acuity.what_to_do_red: If you suddenly lose vision or see a dark area, open the guide now.

vo2max.name: Aerobic fitness (VO₂max)
vo2max.why_it_matters: Fitness drops without exercise in microgravity.
vo2max.what_to_do_red: Your medical team will plan your recovery.

muscle_strength.name: Muscle strength
muscle_strength.why_it_matters: Muscles shrink without load in microgravity.
muscle_strength.what_to_do_red: Your medical team will plan your recovery.

suit_pressure.name: Suit pressure
suit_pressure.why_it_matters: If the suit loses pressure, you must act at once.
suit_pressure.what_to_do_yellow: Check the suit display and tell the crew inside.
suit_pressure.what_to_do_red: Follow your suit emergency procedure and head back to the airlock.

suit_co2.name: Suit CO₂
suit_co2.why_it_matters: Too much CO₂ in the helmet causes headache and slows thinking.
suit_co2.what_to_do_red: Open the purge valve as trained and tell the crew.

eva_time_remaining.name: Time remaining
eva_time_remaining.why_it_matters: Shows how long your oxygen and supplies last.
eva_time_remaining.what_to_do_red: Head back to the airlock now.

suit_temperature.name: Suit temperature
suit_temperature.why_it_matters: Too hot or too cold in the suit affects your body and your work.
suit_temperature.what_to_do_red: Tell the crew and follow your suit procedure.

cabin_co2.name: Cabin CO₂
cabin_co2.why_it_matters: High CO₂ in the air can cause headache and tiredness.
cabin_co2.what_to_do_yellow: Move to a better ventilated area and report it.
cabin_co2.what_to_do_red: Report to the crew and Mission Control; open the guide if you have a headache.

orthostatic_sys_drop.name: Standing test (top number drop)
orthostatic_sys_drop.why_it_matters: After space, blood pools in your legs when you stand, which can make you dizzy or fall.
orthostatic_sys_drop.what_to_do_yellow: Stand up slowly, drink water, have a helper nearby.
orthostatic_sys_drop.what_to_do_red: Sit or lie down now. Do not walk alone. Maia alerts your medical team.
orthostatic_sys_drop.source: S48 (consensus definition, citation NEEDS VALIDATION); S49
